Prealgebra · Lesson 9.4

Percents in Word Problems

Solve this lesson →All lessons

This lesson applies percent-as-fraction, percent of a number, and percent change to word problems. The routine is the same every time. Read the problem and find what whole each percent is taken of, translate the words into a multiplication or a division, solve, then check that the size and direction of your answer make sense.

Problem
A hoodie costs $48$48 and the local sales tax is 7.5%7.5%. How many dollars is the sales tax alone (not the total)?
Show a hint
  • The tax is just 7.5%7.5% OF the price, exactly the kind of "percent of a number" you did in 9.2. The whole is the 48 dollar price and the rate is 7.5%7.5%, so the tax is 7.5%7.5% of 48. Be careful, the question wants the tax by itself, not the 48 plus the tax.
  • Turn the percent into a decimal before multiplying. Since 7.5%=0.0757.5%=0.075, the tax equals 0.075×480.075×48.
Show the full solution
Write 7.5%7.5% as the decimal 0.0750.075 and multiply by the price. 0.075×48=3.60.075×48=3.6 The tax alone is 3.63.6​ dollars. The question asks for the tax by itself, not the total, so there is nothing to add on at the end.
Problem
Four friends have an $80$80 dinner bill and agree on an 18%18% tip. What is the total amount they pay, food plus tip, in dollars?
Show a hint
  • You are paying for the whole meal plus a little extra, so think in one multiplier. You owe all 100%100% of the food and another 18%18% on top, which is 118%118% of the food. Turn 118%118% into a decimal multiplier and you only have to do one multiplication.
  • Multiply the food, 80 dollars, by 1.181.18. If you would rather build it in two pieces, find the tip with 0.18×800.18×80 first, then add that to 80.
Show the full solution
Paying the whole bill plus an 18%18% tip is 118%118% of the food, a multiplier of 1.181.18. 80×1.18=94.4080×1.18=94.40 They pay 94.4094.40​ dollars. Building the tip separately gives the same total, since 0.18×80=14.400.18×80=14.40 and 80+14.40=94.4080+14.40=94.40.
Problem
Mira bought a kettle for $180$180 and marks it up 35%35% of cost. What is the selling price of the kettle in dollars?
Show a hint
  • A markup works exactly like a tax. The selling price is the whole cost plus another 35%35% of that same cost, so it is 100%+35%=135%100%+35%=135% of the cost. Turn that percent into a single multiplier.
  • 135%135% as a decimal is 1.351.35, so the selling price is 180×1.35180×1.35. Multiply that out.
Show the full solution
A 35%35% markup keeps the full cost and adds 35%35% on top, so the selling price is 135%135% of cost, a multiplier of 1.351.35. 180×1.35=243180×1.35=243 The selling price is 243243​ dollars. The markup alone is 0.35×180=630.35×180=63, and 180+63=243180+63=243, the same answer the slow way.
Problem
A longboard is tagged at $240$240. The shop takes 25%25% off, then the register adds 6%6% tax on the reduced price. What is the final price paid in dollars?
Show a hint
  • Handle the two moves one at a time, and notice each one is just a multiplier. Taking 25%25% off keeps the 75%75% that survives, so that step is ×0.75×0.75. Adding 6%6% tax keeps the whole price and piles 6%6% on top, so that step is ×1.06×1.06.
  • Chain the two multipliers in a row rather than doing each as a separate add or subtract. The final price is 240×0.75×1.06240×0.75×1.06. Work left to right, 240×0.75240×0.75 first, then multiply that result by 1.061.06.
Show the full solution
A 25%25% discount leaves 75%75%, so that step is ×0.75×0.75. A 6%6% tax adds on top, so that step is ×1.06×1.06. 240×0.75=180,180×1.06=190.80240×0.75=180,180×1.06=190.80 The final price paid is 190.80190.80​ dollars. The tax rides on the reduced 180, not the original 240. Order does not matter though, since 240×1.06×0.75240×1.06×0.75 lands on the same 190.80.
Key idea
Each percent change is one multiplier. A tax, tip, or markup adds to the full price, so its multiplier is ×(1+rate)×(1+rate). A 9%9% tax means ×1.09×1.09. A discount takes part of the price away, so its multiplier is ×(1−rate)×(1−rate), and 25%25% off means ×0.75×0.75. To find the added or removed amount on its own, use part=rate×pricepart=rate×price. To find the new total, use the multiplier. Several changes multiply in a row, as in price×(1−d)×(1+t)price×(1−d)×(1+t). A product is the same in any order, so taxing first and discounting first give the same price. A total with tax is larger than the price and a sale price is smaller, so check the direction.
Problem
Devon earns a 12%12% commission and sold $1,450$1,450 in glassware on Sunday. How many dollars does Devon earn in commission that day?
Show a hint
  • Commission is a percent OF the sale, so this is a plain "percent of a number" problem. The whole is the 1,4501,450 dollar sale and the rate is 12%12%, so translate the words into 0.12×1,4500.12×1,450.
  • Turn 12%12% into the decimal 0.120.12, then multiply by 1,4501,450. A quick way is to find 10%10% of the sale, which is 145145, then add another 2%2%, which is 2929, and combine them.
Show the full solution
A commission is a percent of the sale. Write 12%12% as 0.120.12 and multiply by the sale. 0.12×1,450=1740.12×1,450=174 Devon earns 174174​ dollars. Split it to check, 10%10% of 1,4501,450 is 145145 and 2%2% is 2929, and 145+29=174145+29=174.
Problem
Naomi earns 8.5%8.5% commission and received $510$510 on one telescope sale. What was the sale price of that telescope in dollars?
Show a hint
  • Name the unknown the sale price and translate the sentence straight across. Her commission is 8.5%8.5% of the sale price, and that commission equals 510510. So 510510 is the part, 8.5%8.5% is the rate, and the sale price is the whole you are hunting for. As an equation that reads 510=0.085×sale510=0.085×sale.
  • You are finding the whole from a part, exactly like in 9.2, so undo the multiplication by dividing. Convert 8.5%8.5% to the decimal 0.0850.085, then compute 510÷0.085510÷0.085. The answer should come out much bigger than 510510, since the commission is only a thin slice of the full price.
Show the full solution
The commission is 8.5%8.5% of the sale price, so 510=0.085×sale510=0.085×sale. Divide the part by the rate. sale=5100.085=6000sale=0.085510​=6000 The telescope sold for 60006000​ dollars. When you know the part and want the whole, you divide, and dividing by a small rate makes the whole far bigger than the part.
Key idea
Part =rate×whole=rate×whole. A commission, a tax, and a tip are each a rate times some whole. To find the part, multiply the rate by the whole, part=rate×wholepart=rate×whole. To find the whole when you know the part, divide the part by the rate, whole=part÷ratewhole=part÷rate. Match each part with its own rate, and never take the rate of the part. Dividing by a small rate gives a bigger number, so if your whole comes out smaller than the part, you divided the wrong way.
Problem
Maple Ridge Middle School cast 320320 ballots on a schedule plan. Of those, 208208 voted in favor. What percent of the votes were in favor of the plan?
Show a hint
  • Decide what is the part and what is the whole. The question asks about the votes in favor, so the part is the 208 in favor and the whole is all 320 votes that were cast. To find what percent one number is of another, set up the part over the whole and turn it into a percent.
  • Compute 208320×100320208​×100. Dividing 208 by 320 gives 0.650.65, and multiplying by 100 turns that decimal into a percent.
Show the full solution
The part is the 208 votes in favor and the whole is all 320 ballots cast. 208320×100=0.65×100=65320208​×100=0.65×100=65 So 6565​ percent voted in favor. The against share is 112320×100=35320112​×100=35, and 65+35=10065+35=100, which is the check worth running on any two-way split.
Problem
A 4040L barrel of mango cooler is 25%25% juice. The owner stirs in 1010 extra liters of plain water, adding no juice. What percent of the new barrel is real mango juice?
Show a hint
  • The amount of mango juice never changes, only water is added. First find how many liters of juice are in the barrel, that is 25%25% of 40, and then find the new total number of liters after the 10 liters of water go in.
  • The new concentration is the juice amount divided by the new total, turned into a percent. Compute 1050×1005010​×100. Since you only added water, expect a number below 25%25%.
Show the full solution
The juice is 0.25×40=100.25×40=10 liters, and pouring in water leaves that 10 liters untouched. The new total is 40+10=5040+10=50 liters, so the juice share is 1050×100=20.5010​×100=20. The barrel is 2020​ percent juice. Adding only water can only weaken the drink, so a number below the original 25%25% is the right direction.
Problem
At a beekeeping challenge, 15%15% of members did not find the queen in time, and that came to exactly 99 members. How many people took the challenge in all?
Show a hint
  • The 9 who missed the queen are not the whole club, they are the slice that failed. Translate the sentence into math, those 9 people are 15%15% of the full group, so 0.150.15 times the group size equals 9. The group size is the whole you are hunting for, the base.
  • You know the part is 9 and its rate is 15%15%, and you want the base. Finding a whole from a part means you divide, so compute 9÷0.159÷0.15.
Show the full solution
The 9 members are the part and 15%15% is the rate, so 0.15×(group size)=90.15×(group size)=9. Divide the part by the rate. 9÷0.15=609÷0.15=60 So 6060​ people took the challenge. Check it forward, 0.15×60=90.15×60=9. Only 15%15% of the group failed, so the whole group has to be much larger than 9.
Key idea
In a two-way split the two percents add to 100%100%. When everyone falls into one of two groups, each group's percent is its own count divided by the total. Since the two add to 100%100%, once you know one you get the other by subtracting. To turn a count into a percent, write counttotal×100totalcount​×100. If you know a count and the percent it makes of the whole, find the whole by dividing, whole=count÷ratewhole=count÷rate. Pair each count with its matching rate, and the whole is bigger than either group.
Problem
A warehouse has 720720 boxes. Monday ships 25%25%. Tuesday ships 40%40% of what remains. Wednesday ships 50%50% of what is left then. How many boxes remain after Wednesday's shipment?
Show a hint
  • Each percent is taken of what is LEFT at that moment, not of the starting 720. So instead of tracking what ships, track the fraction that stays. If 25%25% ships on Monday, then 75%75% stays. If 40%40% of the rest ships on Tuesday, then 60%60% of the rest stays. Turn each step into the leftover multiplier.
  • Multiply the leftover fractions one after another onto 720. That is 720×0.75720×0.75 for Monday, then times 0.600.60 for Tuesday, then times 0.500.50 for Wednesday. The question wants the boxes that REMAIN after Wednesday, not the boxes that were shipped, so the final product is your answer.
Show the full solution
Track what stays instead of what leaves. Monday leaves 75%75%, Tuesday leaves 60%60%, Wednesday leaves 50%50%. 720×0.75=540,540×0.60=324,324×0.50=162720×0.75=540,540×0.60=324,324×0.50=162 After Wednesday, 162162​ boxes remain. Each percent is taken of the current pile, not of the original 720, so the leftover fractions multiply in a chain.
Key idea
When each step takes a percent of what is left, multiply the leftover fractions. A step that acts on what remains uses the reduced amount, not the original. Selling 40%40% leaves 60%60%, and giving away 25%25% of that leaves 75%75% of it. The final amount is the starting amount times every leftover fraction, as in start×0.60×0.75start×0.60×0.75. Do not add the percents removed and subtract once, because each later step takes its percent from a smaller amount.
Fun fact
The per mille sign ‰ means "per thousand", an extra circle on the percent sign. 25‰=2.5%25‰=2.5%. Sea water runs near 35‰35‰ salt. Some countries express blood alcohol limits in per mille.
Problem
The Maple Hollow Otters play a 2525-game season. After 1313 games they have 77 wins. The coach targets a 60%60% win rate for the whole season. How many of the remaining games must they win?
Show a hint
  • First find how many wins the goal needs across the whole season. The target is 60%60% of all 25 games, so translate "60 percent of 25" into multiplication to get the total number of wins the Otters need by the end.
  • They already have 7 of those wins banked. Subtract to see how many more wins they still need, and notice that those extra wins all have to come out of the games that remain.
Show the full solution
A 60%60% win rate over 25 games is 0.60×25=150.60×25=15 wins. They already have 7, so they need 15−7=815−7=8 more, and there are 25−13=1225−13=12 games left to get them. They must win 88​ of their remaining games. Checking, 7+8=157+8=15 wins out of 25 is 1525=35=60%2515​=53​=60%, the target exactly.
Problem
A keyboard is 25%25% off, then 8%8% tax is added to the reduced price. Devansh pays $162$162. What was the original listed price in dollars?
Show a hint
  • Run the story forward first to find the chain. Taking 25 percent off multiplies the listed price by 0.750.75, and adding 8 percent tax multiplies by 1.081.08. So the listed price times 0.750.75 times 1.081.08 equals the 162 he paid. Combine the two multipliers into one number before you do anything else.
  • Since 0.75×1.08=0.810.75×1.08=0.81, the whole deal is just listed price times 0.81=1620.81=162. You are given the result and want the starting number, so undo the multiply by dividing. Compute 162÷0.81162÷0.81.
Show the full solution
A 25%25% discount is ×0.75×0.75 and an 8%8% tax is ×1.08×1.08, so listed×0.75×1.08=162listed×0.75×1.08=162. Since 0.75×1.08=0.810.75×1.08=0.81, divide to undo it. listed=1620.81=200listed=0.81162​=200 The original listed price was 200200​ dollars. Running it forward confirms the chain, 200×0.75=150200×0.75=150 and 150×1.08=162150×1.08=162.

Practice these ideas

Practice
A kettle sells for $60$60 and a 5%5% sales tax is added. How many dollars is the sales tax alone?
Show the solution
Write 5%5% as the decimal 0.050.05 and multiply by the 60 dollar price. 0.05×60=30.05×60=3 The sales tax alone is 33​ dollars. The total with tax would be 63 dollars, but the question asked only for the tax, so stop at 3.
Practice
A ukulele is listed at $150$150 before 6%6% sales tax. What is the total amount you pay including the tax?
Show the solution
Adding 6%6% tax means multiplying by 1+0.06=1.061+0.06=1.06. 150×1.06=159150×1.06=159 You pay 159159​ dollars. The tax on its own is 0.06×150=90.06×150=9, and 150+9=159150+9=159, the same total.
Practice
Naomi's grooming bill is $40$40 and she adds a 15%15% tip. How many dollars does Naomi pay in all?
Show the solution
A 15%15% tip means paying 115%115% of the bill, a multiplier of 1.151.15. 40×1.15=4640×1.15=46 Naomi pays 4646​ dollars in all. The tip by itself is 0.15×40=60.15×40=6 dollars, and 40+6=4640+6=46.
Practice
Mara earns 5%5% commission and closed a $2400$2400 solar job. How much does she earn in commission, in dollars?
Show the solution
Commission is a percent of the sale. Write 5%5% as 0.050.05 and multiply by the job. 0.05×2400=1200.05×2400=120 Mara earns 120120​ dollars in commission. Ten percent of 2400 is 240, and 5%5% is half of that, which is 120.
Practice
Priya earns 9%9% commission and received $630$630 on one kayak sale. What was the sale price of that kayak in dollars?
Show the solution
The 9%9% commission on the sale price came to 630 dollars, so 0.09×price=6300.09×price=630. Divide the part by the rate. price=6300.09=7000price=0.09630​=7000 The kayak sold for 70007000​ dollars. Check it forward, 0.09×7000=6300.09×7000=630, and the price should come out far larger than the commission.
Practice
A garden center pays $90$90 for a planter and marks it up 40%40%. What is the shelf price in dollars?
Show the solution
A 40%40% markup makes the shelf price 140%140% of what the store paid, a multiplier of 1.401.40. 90×1.40=12690×1.40=126 The shelf price is 126126​ dollars. The markup alone is 0.40×90=360.40×90=36, and 90+36=12690+36=126.
Practice
A peacoat is priced at $220$220 and marked 15%15% off. What is the discounted price Devang pays in dollars?
Show the solution
A 15%15% discount leaves 100%−15%=85%100%−15%=85% of the price, a multiplier of 0.850.85. 220×0.85=187220×0.85=187 Devang pays 187187​ dollars. The discount itself is 0.15×220=330.15×220=33 dollars, and 220−33=187220−33=187.
Practice
A desk lamp is priced at $250$250. The shop takes 10%10% off, then rings up 8%8% tax on the reduced price. What is the final price paid in dollars?
Show the solution
A 10%10% discount leaves 90%90%, so multiply by 0.900.90. Then 8%8% tax on the reduced price multiplies by 1.081.08. 250×0.90=225,225×1.08=243250×0.90=225,225×1.08=243 The final price paid is 243243​ dollars. The tax is charged on the reduced 225, not the original 250, which is why the chain reads 250×0.90×1.08250×0.90×1.08.
Practice
A lending library has 8484 books, and 2121 were checked out on the weekend. What percent of the library's books were checked out?
Show the solution
The part is the 21 books checked out and the whole is all 84 books. 2184×100=14×100=258421​×100=41​×100=25 So 2525​ percent of the books were checked out. A quarter of 84 is 21, which matches the count that left the shelves.
Practice
A robotics club of 200200 members voted on practice time. Exactly 140140 voted for mornings. What percent voted for evenings? Give the number only.
Show the solution
With only two choices, the evening voters are the 200−140=60200−140=60 members left over. Compare that count to the whole club. 60200=0.3020060​=0.30 so 3030​ percent voted for evenings. Divide by the total membership, never by the 140 on the other side. The morning share is 70%70%, and the two add to 100%100%.
Practice
Exactly 20%20% of people who sat a certification exam did not pass, and that group numbered 1212. How many people took the exam in all?
Show the solution
The 12 who did not pass are 20%20% of the whole group, so 0.20×total=120.20×total=12. Divide the part by the rate. total=120.20=60total=0.2012​=60 So 6060​ people took the exam. Check it forward, 0.20×60=120.20×60=12, and the other 80%80% is 48 passers, with 48+12=6048+12=60.
Practice
A crew prints 600600 flyers. They hand out 20%20% to passersby. Then rain ruins 25%25% of the flyers still in the box. How many flyers does the crew have left?
Show the solution
Handing out 20%20% leaves 80%80% in the box, and the rain ruining 25%25% leaves 75%75% of what was still there. 600×0.80=480,480×0.75=360600×0.80=480,480×0.75=360 The crew has 360360​ flyers left. That 25%25% comes off the 480 in the box, not off the original 600, so the leftover fractions multiply rather than the losses adding up.
Practice
An 8080L barrel of polishing fluid is 25%25% solvent. An apprentice stirs in 2020 more liters of plain water. What percent of the new mixture is solvent? Give the number only.
Show the solution
The solvent is 0.25×80=200.25×80=20 liters, and plain water adds none of it. The total grows to 80+20=10080+20=100 liters, so the solvent share is 20100×100=20.10020​×100=20. The new mixture is 2020​ percent solvent. Compare the solvent to the whole new mixture, and expect a number below 25%25% since only water went in.
Practice
The Marlowe Middle quiz bowl team plays a 2828-game season. After 1616 games they have 99 wins. They want a 50%50% win rate for the whole season. How many of their remaining games must they win?
Show the solution
A 50%50% season needs 12×28=1421​×28=14 wins in all. They have 9, so they still need 14−9=514−9=5. The team must win 55​ of its remaining games. There are 28−16=1228−16=12 games left, so 5 is well within reach, and 9+5=149+5=14 out of 28 is exactly 50%50%.

Learn it by doing it

Reading is a start. In the course you solve each problem yourself, with instant feedback, layered hints, and Milo right beside you when you get stuck.
